name: False Nine 4-3-3

slots.why: Sweeper keeper is an extra passer in build-up and covers the space behind a higher line.
Support full-back gives width while the inverted wingers move inside.
Ball-playing defender starts moves with progressive passes through the press.
Central defender who defends while his partner plays. Cover is the alternate.
Support full-back on the right, doing the same job as on the left.
Supporting holding midfielder screens the defence and gives the midfield a passing base.
Box-to-box midfielder runs into the space the false nine vacates and supports the counter-press.
Advanced playmaker is the creative centre of the midfield and links with the false nine.
Inverted winger starts wide and cuts inside, running into the space the false nine leaves and attacking the far post.
Inverted winger on the right, mirroring the left so both centre-back gaps are attacked.
False nine drops between the lines to link play and pulls a centre-back out of position.

description: A possession 4-3-3 whose striker drops into midfield, dragging a centre-back with him and leaving space for two inverted wingers to run into from wide.
whyGood: The false nine adds a spare man in midfield, so the team outnumbers the opponent's midfield while the wingers attack the space he leaves behind.
whyThisShape: Dropping the striker into midfield gives you a spare man against the opponent's midfield, and it puts the opposition centre-back in a dilemma: follow him and leave a gap, or stay and let him receive. The two inverted wingers start wide and run into the centre-back's space, so the attack comes from the sides of the box rather than from a striker in the middle.
whenToUse: Against a back four that defends deep and narrow, when you have a striker who is a better passer than a finisher and two wingers who can score.
whenNotToUse: Against a back three, or a side that keeps its centre-backs in position, since there is no gap to exploit; and when your wingers cannot finish, since nobody is left in the box.

instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Keeps the ball in tight triangles, which is how the false nine and midfield combine.
instructionRationale.Play Out Of Defence: The sweeper keeper and ball-playing defender build from the back so the midfield can receive under little pressure.
instructionRationale.Work Ball Into Box: Patient combinations until a run behind the pulled-out centre-back opens up.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Presses at once after losing the ball, since many players are close to it.
instructionRationale.Higher Line of Engagement: Presses in the opponent's half to keep the play high and the ball near the forwards.
instructionRationale.Higher Defensive Line: Keeps the team compact around the ball; it needs a keeper who sweeps and defenders with pace.

keyRequirements: A forward who passes and dribbles better than he finishes
Two wingers who cut in and score
A sweeper keeper who is comfortable on the ball
